overview:
Darin LaHood seeks another term in a central Illinois district that leans Republican by about eleven points. He has raised $3.7 million and holds $6.7 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Paul Nolley has raised about $416,000 with $230,000 available, leaving a large resource gap. No outside groups are meaningfully engaged in the race.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the contest, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money, all of which favor LaHood. Prediction markets give him roughly a 95 percent chance of winning. The race is rated Safe R, with a modest chance of an upset if the political environment shifts sharply against Republicans.
